transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Ever since that near-crash on the plane, every small noise or movement makes me jump out of my skin. I just can’t function in meetings anymore because I’m constantly on edge, waiting for something bad to happen.
How long have these symptoms been going on since the plane incident? Have they lasted more than a month?
No, it hasn't been a month—the near-crash was actually just six days ago. All of this started immediately after we landed and has been going on continuously ever since.
Have you also been feeling persistently sad, hopeless, or unable to enjoy things since the incident, or is it mainly the jumpiness and feeling on edge?

While the jumpiness is exhausting, I also feel completely numb and unable to enjoy anything. It feels like a switch flipped inside me—even when my wife shares good news about our kids or the company hits a target, I just sit there numb. I feel like I'm watching someone else's life without any joy or warmth at all.
Since the plane incident, have you had unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about what happened, or felt like you were reliving it?

Yes, all week these vivid scenes just slam into my head out of nowhere—the masks dropping, the flight attendant hitting the ceiling, and people screaming. For a few seconds, I feel like I'm right back in that seat, sweating and gripping my armrests like we're about to die again, even if I'm just sitting at my desk at work.
Have you been having repeated nightmares or flashbacks where it feels like the plane incident is happening again, or are the symptoms mainly feeling jumpy and numb?

Yes, I am definitely experiencing both. Those terrifying scenes of the masks dropping and people screaming slam into my head, making me feel like I'm right back in my seat sweating and gripping the armrests. At the same time, I'm constantly jumpy—startled by small noises like a passing truck or a chair rolling—and completely numb to any good news.
Have these symptoms been going on for less than a month, or have they continued for more than a month since the plane incident?

Yes, it has been less than a month—the flight was actually just six days ago. All of these symptoms started immediately after we landed and have been going on continuously every single day since. It's incredibly distressing how quickly my life has collapsed in less than a week.
Have you ever had a similar traumatic event before this flight, or is this the first time you’ve had these kinds of symptoms after a trauma?
No, I have never been through a traumatic event like this before. These symptoms are entirely new to me, and I've never experienced anything like this in my life.
Have these symptoms been happening for less than a month, or have they continued for more than a month since the plane incident?
It has definitely been less than a month, as the plane incident happened just six days ago. These feelings started immediately after we landed and have been going on continuously ever since.
Have you had any periods of feeling back to normal since the plane incident, or have the symptoms been present almost every day since it happened?

No, I haven't had any periods of feeling back to normal at all. It has been completely continuous every single day since the flight six days ago. I am on edge from the moment I wake up until I try to go to sleep.
Since the plane incident, have you felt detached from yourself or your surroundings, like things are unreal or you are watching everything happen from outside your body?

Yes, absolutely. Especially at the office or lying in bed at night, I feel like I'm watching myself from across the room and the world looks flat and unreal. It's like I'm stuck in a bad movie of that flight and haven't fully returned to my own body yet.
Have your symptoms been getting better, staying the same, or getting worse over the past few days since the flight?

They haven't improved at all; if anything, they feel just as intense and overwhelming as they did the day we landed. Every single day has been a constant struggle, and I feel just as on edge and paralyzed by this now as I did right after the flight.
Have these symptoms been present for less than a month, or have they continued for more than a month since the plane incident?
It has been less than a month, as the plane incident was only six days ago. These symptoms have been going on continuously every single day since then.
Have you had these symptoms for less than a month since the plane incident, or have they continued for more than a month?
It has definitely been less than a month, as the near-crash happened just six days ago. These symptoms have been going on continuously ever since that day.
Just to confirm, did these symptoms begin immediately after the plane incident and have they been present continuously for less than one month so far?
Yes, that is exactly right. Everything started immediately after the near-crash six days ago, and it has been going on continuously every single day since then.

Since the plane incident, have you noticed that the symptoms are gradually easing, or are they still just as intense and constant every day? Also, are you having any nightmares or flashbacks that make it feel like the event is happening again?

No, they haven't eased at all; they are still just as intense and constant every single day. I keep having flashbacks where I am suddenly right back in that seat, sweating and gripping the armrests as if we're about to crash. It just slams into my head out of nowhere, with vivid memories of the masks dropping and people screaming.
Have these symptoms been present for less than one month since the plane incident, or have they continued for more than one month?
Yes, it has been less than a month, as the plane incident happened just six days ago. These feelings have been completely constant and intense every single day since then.
Have these symptoms lasted continuously for more than one month, or are they still within the first month after the traumatic event?
They are definitely still within the first month, as the near-crash was only six days ago. It has been a continuous struggle, but it hasn't even been a full week yet.
Just to confirm, have these symptoms been going on for less than a month since the plane incident, or have they continued for more than a month?
It has been less than a month, as the incident was only six days ago. All of this started immediately after we landed and has been going on continuously since then, so it's been less than a week.
Have you been having repeated nightmares or flashbacks where it feels like the plane incident is happening again, or are your symptoms mainly feeling jumpy and numb?

I am absolutely experiencing both. I have intense flashbacks where those terrifying scenes slam into my head and I'm suddenly right back in that seat sweating and gripping the armrests, while in my daily life I feel completely numb and constantly jumpy at every little sound.
Have your symptoms been improving at all, or are they still severe and continuous? Also, have they lasted longer than one month since the plane incident?
No, they haven't improved at all and remain incredibly severe and constant. It has not been a month yet since the incident only happened six days ago, but the distress has been continuous ever since.
Have your symptoms been present for more than one month since the plane incident, or are they still within the first month?
They are definitely still within the first month, as the near-crash happened only six days ago. It has been less than a week, though the constant intensity of it makes it feel much longer.
Did you have any symptoms during the first month after the flight that were mainly a mix of shock, dissociation, and anxiety, and then did the symptoms continue beyond a month?

The flight actually happened just six days ago, so it has not been a month yet. Since the incident, though, I have been experiencing intense anxiety, shock, and constant feelings of being disconnected and unreal.
Have these symptoms lasted less than one month since the plane incident, or have they continued for more than one month?
It has been less than a month, as the near-crash was only six days ago. These feelings have been constant and continuous since that day.
Just to confirm, have these symptoms been happening for less than one month since the plane incident, or have they continued for more than one month?
Yes, it has been less than a month because the near-crash was only six days ago. Everything started immediately after we landed and has been going on continuously since then.
Have these symptoms lasted continuously for more than one month since the plane incident, or are they still within the first month?
They are definitely still within the first month, as the near-crash was only six days ago. It has been less than a week since it happened, so we are nowhere near the one-month mark yet.
Just to confirm, did these symptoms start within a month of the plane incident and have they lasted less than a month total so far?
Yes, that is correct. They started immediately after the flight six days ago and have been going on continuously ever since. So yes, it has been less than a week total so far.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient developed acute traumatic stress symptoms immediately after a qualifying plane near-crash, including intrusive flashbacks, marked startle/jumpiness, persistent anxiety/hypervigilance, emotional numbing, and dissociative symptoms (depersonalization/derealization). Symptoms began within hours of the event and have lasted only 6 days, which fits acute stress reaction rather than a longer-duration trauma-related disorder.
